newsitem.title: USA: Novavax study shows product cuts hot flashes.
newsitem.headline: Novavax study shows product cuts hot flashes.

text.p: Novavax Inc said Wednesday its experimental estrogen reduced hot flashes up to 98 percent during a two-week study of 10 post menopausal women.
The company said it considers results of the study important because they are a formal indication of the potential benefits of a "patchless" transdermal version of natural human estrogen.
The company said topically applied experimental product contains the active hormone in a cosmetic-like cream, sidestepping certain disadvantages of skin patches.
The company said the new product candidate, called Estrasorb, was designed to reduce the occurrence of hot flashes in menopausal and post menopausal women.
Hot flashes, in which women experience a sensation of heat with perspiration and some reddening of the skin, are considered a side effect of menopause.
The company said its findings came from the first phase of a dose- ranging study approved two months ago by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The study showed a 69-98 percent reduction of hot flashes during the second week of 14 consecutive days of Estrasorb administration.
The company said Estrasorb was well tolerated by the study group and there were no signs of skin irritation.
Skin irritation is a reported side effect of most transdermal patches, and often inhibits their use during hot or humid weather.
Additional studies are ongoing to determine the most appropriate dose of the product for women in need of estrogen replacement therapy for control of menopausal and post menopausal symptoms.
